item.title: HIV: Lagos survey reveals treatment gains, testing gap
item.description: … Women record twice men’s prevalence as state targets wider coverage By Chioma Obinna Lagos State has recorded significant progress in HIV treatment, with 93.4 per cent of people living with the virus who know their status receiving antiretroviral therapy (ART), a new survey has revealed. However, only 58.3 per cent of people living with HIV know their status, highlighting a major testing gap that could undermine efforts to control the epidemic. The 2025–2026 Antiretroviral Therapy (ART) Impact Survey also found that HIV prevalence among adults aged 15 to 64 was twice as high among women as men, at 1.6 per cent and 0.8 per cent, respectively. The findings were presented at the dissemination of the Lagos State Summary Sheet of the survey at the Sheraton Hotel, Ikeja, on Wednesday. The survey has prompted renewed calls for intensified HIV testing, improved access to treatment and sustainable funding to close existing gaps in the state’s response. Speaking at the event, the Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Ministry of Health, Dr Dayo Lajide, described the survey as an important milestone in strengthening the state’s HIV response through credible evidence and informed decision-making. She said the findings would help assess progress since the 2018 Nigeria HIV/AIDS Indicator and Impact Survey and support efforts towards achieving the UNAIDS 95-95-95 targets. Lajide disclosed that “the 2025 HIV Health Sector Report estimated that 192,911 people were living with HIV in Lagos, while 129,977 were receiving antiretroviral therapy, representing 65.7 per cent treatment coverage and leaving more than 60,000 people outside treatment.” She also highlighted gaps in services for mothers and children, noting that although prevention of mother-to-child transmission coverage increased from 45 per cent in 2018 to 57.6 per cent in 2025, early infant diagnosis and paediatric treatment remained areas of concern. The Permanent Secretary called for targeted interventions to improve case identification, treatment linkage, retention in care and services for children exposed to HIV. She reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to sustaining services through the procurement of rapid diagnostic kits and antiretroviral medicines, strengthening health systems and integrating HIV services into routine healthcare. Lajide also stressed the need for domestic resource mobilisation and sustainable financing amid changes in the global healthcare funding landscape. Presenting the survey findings, APIN/PHIS3 Survey Lead, Dr Ubong Okon, said the assessment examined HIV prevalence, testing, treatment access and viral load suppression. Conducted between November 2025 and February 2026, the survey covered 205 enumeration areas and 6,450 households. Okon disclosed that 93.5 per cent of the 6,748 eligible households completed household interviews. item.title: Tinubu congratulates Zenith Bank founder Jim Ovia on his 75th birthday
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA–PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has congratulated Mr. Jim Ovia, the founder and Chairman of Zenith Bank Plc, on his 75th birthday. President Tinubu commended Ovia’s remarkable contributions to Nigeria’s banking industry, economic development and private-sector growth, describing him as a visionary entrepreneur, accomplished banker and distinguished business leader. “Mr. Ovia’s dedication, resilience and commitment to excellence have not only grown Zenith Bank into a banking behemoth but also helped the growth of the Nigerian financial services sector. “His pioneering role in establishing Zenith Bank in the 90s and building it into one of Nigeria’s leading financial institutions, with significant presence across Africa, Europe and beyond is remarkable,” the President said. President Tinubu affirmed that Ovia’s entrepreneurial journey reflects the importance of innovation, discipline, sound corporate governance and long-term investment in national development. The President also laudsled his contributions to digital infrastructure, awareness and inclusion, education, youth empowerment, philanthropy and human capital development, particularly through initiatives that create opportunities for young Nigerians to achieve their potential. As Mr. Ovia marks this milestone, President Tinubu wished him continued good health, strength and more years of productive service to Nigeria and humanity. item.title: Kwara converts Omu-Aran General Hospital to teaching hospital
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin Kwara State Governor, AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, on Wednesday laid the foundation for the conversion of the General Hospital, Omu-Aran, into the Thomas Adewumi University Teaching Hospital under a public-private partnership arrangement aimed at expanding access to specialised healthcare in Kwara South. The project is expected to strengthen medical education, improve healthcare manpower development and reduce the burden on existing tertiary health facilities in the state. Speaking at the foundation-laying ceremony, the governor, who was represented by his deputy, Kayode Alabi, described the initiative as a milestone in the development of healthcare infrastructure in Kwara South. “Today marks another milestone as we witness the establishment of the first Teaching Hospital in Kwara South. This remarkable achievement, conceived and actualised through a strategic partnership with the Kwara State Government through the Ministry of Health, will deeply promote medical education, improve human resources in health and contribute significantly to increasing access to quality healthcare delivery for our people,” he said. AbdulRazaq said establishing a tertiary healthcare facility in the southern part of the state would decentralise specialised medical services and reduce pressure on centrally located hospitals, which residents often find difficult to access. He expressed confidence that the facility would contribute to reducing preventable deaths and improving healthcare outcomes across communities. The governor said the project reflected his administration’s commitment to partnerships with private stakeholders to accelerate development, adding that upgrading the existing facility would bring medical services closer to residents of Omu-Aran and neighbouring communities. He commended the founder, management, staff and students of Thomas Adewumi University for their commitment to medical education and development, while urging residents of Omu-Aran to support the project. In his remarks, the Founder and Chancellor of Thomas Adewumi University, Engr. Johnson Bamidele Adewumi, said the former General Hospital, established on February 1, 1973, by the administration of the late General David Bamigboye, offered an opportunity to expand specialised healthcare services in Kwara South. He said the university adopted the teaching hospital project as part of its vision to train medical doctors and other allied health professionals. Adewumi explained that rather than establish an entirely new facility, the university approached the state government with a proposal to transform the existing hospital through a strategic partnership. item.title: Nasarawa APC crisis: Govt calls for probe of rally disruption
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has called on security agencies to investigate an incident that reportedly disrupted activities surrounding Vice-President Kashim Shettima’s visit to the Emir of Lafia during Wednesday’s All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally. The government made the call following reports of disturbances during the Vice-President’s visit to the traditional ruler and allegations of an incident involving Governor Abdullahi Sule at the rally held at Lafia Square. The governor’s Personal Assistant on Social Media, Emmanuel Innocent Akwe, had raised concerns over the incident, alleging that the governor was pelted with objects suspected to be stones by some aggrieved party members. In a statement, Akwe described the reported incident as unacceptable and called for respect for the office of the governor and the unity of the APC in the state. The state government subsequently expressed concern over the reported disruption of the Vice-President’s visit to the Emir, urging security agencies to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident. The Secretary to the State Government, Labaran Magaji, who made the government’s position known in a statement, said Shettima had visited the traditional ruler as a mark of respect for the traditional institution. He regretted that the visit was reportedly disrupted by actions he described as disrespectful to constituted authorities and the office of the Vice-President. Magaji urged security agencies to conduct a thorough investigation, identify those responsible for any wrongdoing and ensure that anyone found culpable was dealt with in accordance with the law. The development comes amid political disagreements within the state chapter of the APC following the party’s recent governorship primary. However, the circumstances surrounding the reported disturbances and the identities of those responsible have yet to be independently established. As of the time of filing this report, there had been no official clarification on the allegations surrounding the incidents. item.title: NACCIMA honours NAFDAC DG, hails war on fake drugs
item.description: …Adeyeye highlights reforms to boost industry, protect public health By Daniel Kudayah The Director-General of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), Prof. Mojisola Christianah Adeyeye, has received an Award of Excellent Performance from the Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture (NACCIMA) in recognition of her contributions to industrial growth and the fight against fake and substandard drugs. The award was presented at NACCIMA’s Breakfast Roundtable Meeting held at Providence Hotel, Lagos, where Adeyeye served as guest speaker. The meeting brought together members of the association, captains of industry and key stakeholders from the organised private sector to discuss regulatory processes, business growth and public health protection. In her keynote address, Adeyeye highlighted regulatory reforms introduced under her leadership, emphasising NAFDAC’s commitment to transparent, science-driven and business-friendly regulation. She explained that the agency’s regulatory framework was designed to support industrial growth while ensuring that only safe, quality and wholesome products reach Nigerian consumers. Industry leaders and other participants at the meeting commended the NAFDAC boss for her leadership, particularly her efforts to combat fake and substandard drugs and her contributions to creating a more supportive regulatory environment for businesses. They praised her commitment to safeguarding public health while promoting the growth and development of industries in Nigeria. The award, according to NACCIMA, recognised Adeyeye’s outstanding performance, hard work and contributions to industry and the fight against counterfeit and substandard products. The presentation was greeted with applause from participants at the event. NAFDAC, under Adeyeye’s leadership, has continued to pursue measures aimed at strengthening the regulation of food, drugs and other regulated products, with the dual objective of protecting consumers and supporting legitimate businesses. The recognition by NACCIMA underscores the importance of collaboration between regulators and the organised private sector in promoting product quality, consumer safety and sustainable industrial development. item.title: Hamzat seeks stronger private sector role in Lagos development
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — Lagos State Deputy Governor and All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 election, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, has called for stronger public-private sector collaboration, improved revenue generation and sustained infrastructure investment to drive the state’s long-term development. Hamzat made the call on Wednesday at an investment management engagement tagged, “The Exclusive Investment Parley with Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat”, organised by Aztran Company on Lagos Island. He said governance was more complex than running a private business because government institutions had to cater to everyone while managing competing social and economic demands. “Governance is far more complex than running a private business because the government does not have the luxury of choosing who it serves; it must serve everyone. That is why strengthening public-private sector collaboration is critical to delivering sustainable development for Lagos,” he said. Comparing Lagos State’s N4.4 trillion budget with New York City’s $109 billion budget, Hamzat said the next phase of development in Lagos required sustaining existing investments and expanding the resources available for infrastructure delivery. He said the state government had recorded achievements in socioeconomic and political development, citing the successful implementation of 11 Oracle Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) modules. According to him, the reforms improved financial accountability, eliminated ghost workers and revenue leakages, and significantly boosted the state’s internally generated revenue. Hamzat also cited the state’s ability to finance major infrastructure projects, including rail development, as evidence of its capacity to execute complex projects despite limited resources. On waste management, the deputy governor reaffirmed the government’s commitment to reforming the sector through improved funding arrangements, efficient waste collection and increased support for Private Sector Participants (PSPs). He explained that the government was reviewing the existing collection model to enable PSP operators to receive payments directly from the government rather than depending solely on collections from residents. He added that subsidies would be sustained to cushion the impact of rising operational costs on waste management operators. Earlier, the Co-Managing Partner of Aztran, Victor Aluyi, called for deeper collaboration between the private sector and the Lagos State Government, urging investors to mobilise capital to bridge the state’s infrastructure financing gap. Aluyi said government funding alone could not meet Lagos’ growing infrastructure needs, particularly in mass transportation, power, affordable housing, waste management and logistics. He put Lagos’ estimated Gross Domestic Product at $260 billion, describing it as Africa’s second-largest city economy after Cairo. item.title: Judicial Misconduct: NJC suspends 3 judges, places 6 on watchlist
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri The National Judicial Council (NJC) has suspended three judges for one year over alleged judicial misconduct, with two of them also barred from promotion for three years. The Council, which took the decision at its 112th meeting held on November 3 under the chairmanship of the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, also placed six other judges on its watchlist and issued them a warning. A late-night statement by the Deputy Director (Information) at the NJC, Kemi Babalola-Ogedengbe, further revealed that, aside from dismissing 24 petitions that levelled sundry allegations against judges across the federation, the Council approved the appointment of 28 judicial officers and recommended four petitions for further investigation. Babalola-Ogedengbe disclosed that Justice Hannatu Mohammed Kabir of the Nasarawa State High Court was suspended for one year without pay and barred from elevation for three years over the unlawful detention of a litigant for 58 days without proper contempt proceedings. “The Investigation Committee found that she ordered the litigant’s arrest and detention for alleged disobedience of court orders without the issuance and service of the mandatory Forms 48 and 49 or the institution of proper contempt proceedings. “It held that the alleged contempt occurred outside the court’s presence and could not lawfully be summarily tried and punished. The Committee also found that the action violated the litigant’s right to fair hearing,” the statement added. Likewise, the Grand Kadi of the Jigawa State Sharia Court of Appeal, Mohammed Sani Salihu, was suspended without pay over his involvement in reopening a judgment delivered by the FCT Upper Area Court. The Committee found that the Grand Kadi exceeded his authority by constituting a committee to review the judgment and subsequently assigning the matter to a Higher Sharia Court Judge, who received fresh evidence and delivered another judgment. The Committee held that the process amounted to an appeal against a valid judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction. The new judgment was subsequently set aside by the Jigawa State High Court. The Committee also found the act to constitute a violation of Rule 3.3.1 of the Revised Code of Conduct for Judicial Officers, 2016. The NJC directed that the most senior Kadi of the Jigawa State Sharia Court of Appeal should perform the functions of the office of the Grand Kadi for the period of the suspension. For his part, Justice Sobere Biambo of the Rivers State High Court was suspended, with a restriction placed on his promotion, after it was found that he issued bench warrants and imposed fines on litigants in a civil dispute without due process. item.title: Google turns off AI for schoolchildren by default
item.description: Google has said it will switch off its AI tools for schoolchildren by default, after drawing criticism for pushing artificial intelligence features to students while schools are still debating how the technology should be used in classrooms. The search engine juggernaut dominates technology in American schools. Its education apps, including Gmail, Docs and the Classroom platform, are used in classrooms across the country, and its low-cost Chromebook laptops are the devices US schools most often issue to students. Under the changes Google announced in a blog post on Tuesday, Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Search will be turned off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators switch them on. Google told AFP the new controls would be rolled out worldwide, beginning in the United States, but that it had not yet set a date. The changes also mean schools will not be able to give students Google Search without its AI features. Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president for education, told The New York Times that “Search and A.I. are deeply integrated,” as AI features are now built into the company’s search engine. If a school bans AI, he said, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.” New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused Google on X of “trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools.” “No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children,” he wrote. More than 150 million students worldwide use Google Classroom, according to a letter Senators Richard Blumenthal and Josh Hawley sent to the company last month asking why AI features had been made the default on school devices. In August, Google opened its Gemini chatbot in Classroom to students of all ages. Students were shown starter prompts tied to their specific class and assignment, offering guided help or study guides, practice quizzes and flashcards built from their course materials. The feature was switched on by default for students at schools that had already enabled Gemini. New York and Los Angeles both announced plans in September to restrict access to AI tools on school devices. “We are reviewing Google’s announcement and its potential implications for schools, educators and students,” a spokesperson for the Los Angeles Unified School District told AFP. The spokesperson said the district believes AI can improve teaching and learning if it is introduced carefully and with clear safeguards, and pointed to district principles requiring that technology support rather than replace teachers and protect student privacy. In a statement on X, Google said Tuesday’s changes give “schools more choice, not less.” “We know there’s concern about students using AI to shortcut schoolwork, and schools have told us they want control,” Google said. item.title: Nigerian footballer Quadri Liameed discharged from hospital after head kick in Spain
item.description: Nigerian midfielder Quadri Liameed has been discharged from hospital after medical tests ruled out serious injuries following a head kick during Sabadell’s match against Albacete in Spain. The 24-year-old initially lost consciousness after being struck in the head by Albacete player José Corpas during the 43rd minute of the encounter at the Carlos Belmonte Stadium. Liameed later regained consciousness and was taken to hospital for medical examinations, raising concerns among his teammates, club officials and football supporters. However, Sabadell confirmed that the midfielder had received medical clearance shortly after midnight after further tests returned reassuring results. In a statement published on its official X account, the club said, “The best of the news has arrived! “@Qlimeed has received medical discharge after all the tests have come out well and will return tonight to Sabadell! “We want to thank the medical services of @AlbaceteBPSAD for the help received at all times.” The midfielder returned to Sabadell by car, accompanied by a member of the club’s medical staff, and went home to rest. According to reports, the concussion protocol was deactivated after the medical examinations ruled out any injury, meaning he did not need to remain under observation overnight. Liameed is expected to follow a specialised training programme over the next few days before fully rejoining his teammates. The incident occurred after Corpas struck Liameed in the head with his boot while attempting to reach the ball, prompting an immediate medical response and his subsequent removal from the pitch. item.title: Kekere-Ekun to chair presentation of Pinheiro’s 6 legal publications
item.description: By Innocent Anaba The Chief Justice of Nigeria, CJN, Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, will chair the public presentation of six legal books authored by Dr ‘Kemi Pinheiro, SAN, on November 20, 2026. The publications, which draw on Pinheiro’s nearly four decades of legal practice, examine critical areas of Nigerian law, including criminal litigation, arbitration, corporate insolvency, justice administration and emerging legal issues. The collection comprises Strategies in Criminal Trial: A Practitioner’s Guide; Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure; Arbitration Law and Practice in Nigeria; Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk (Volume One); The Compendium; and MULAN Legal: Trending Issues of Law and Faith – Essays in Honour of ‘Kemi Pinheiro, SAN. The book on criminal trials examines key procedural and evidential issues in criminal proceedings, including the treatment and admissibility of electronic evidence. Similarly, Insolvency Law in Nigeria: Practice and Procedure explores the legal framework governing corporate rescue, restructuring and insolvency proceedings under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020. Arbitration Law and Practice in Nigeria examines the country’s arbitration framework, with particular attention to the Arbitration and Mediation Act 2023 and the enforcement of arbitral awards. It also addresses the growing importance of alternative dispute resolution in settling commercial disputes. Beyond these practice-oriented publications, Defining Moments: Chronicles of a Silk (Volume One) chronicles Pinheiro’s professional journey and experiences in the legal profession. The Compendium features scholarly essays by legal practitioners and academics, while MULAN Legal: Trending Issues of Law and Faith – Essays in Honour of ‘Kemi Pinheiro, SAN examines the intersection of law, faith and Nigeria’s plural legal system through contributions from various authors. The six publications bring together practical legal guidance, academic research and professional reflections on the development of Nigerian law, with subject matter relevant to judges, legal practitioners, academics and other stakeholders in the administration of justice. The public presentation, organised by Pinheiro LP, is expected to attract members of the judiciary, the Bar, academia and other stakeholders in the legal profession. item.title: 2027: Atiku Vows To Tackle Insecurity At Sokoto Campaign Flag-Off, Says Nothing Will Stop ADC
item.description: Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has reaffirmed his commitment to tackling insecurity, declaring that alleged attempts to frustrate his party’s campaign will not stop its activities ahead of the 2027 general election. “I enumerated some of the promises I made to Nigerians. One of the promises is to make sure that security is restored in every part of this country.” ﻿ Atiku spoke on Wednesday at the flag-off of his presidential campaign in Sokoto, where he urged Nigerians to support the ADC and vote for the party in the forthcoming election. His declaration came a day after he accused the Sokoto State Government and security operatives of plotting to disrupt the campaign rally, alleging that the Department of State Services (DSS) was recruiting protesters to cause disturbances and create a situation that could be used to impose a curfew. Crowd at the flag off of Atiku Abubakar campaign in Sokoto on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. At a news conference in Abuja on Tuesday, the former Vice President also accused the state government of denying the ADC access to public facilities and logistical support for the rally. He described the alleged restrictions as deliberate attempts to deny the opposition party a level playing field. The DSS subsequently ordered an investigation into Atiku’s allegation, saying the directive was issued by its Director-General despite the Service describing the claim as inconsistent with its operations. In its response, the agency said its operatives had provided security protection to political actors across party lines. It cited an incident involving the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto, Mannir Daniya, whom its personnel reportedly evacuated to safety after he was attacked on October 31. Despite the controversy, Atiku proceeded with the campaign flag-off, saying no attempt to frustrate the party would deter it from addressing the people of Sokoto. Crowd at the flag off of Atiku Abubakar campaign in Sokoto on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. He explained that the state was deliberately chosen for the campaign launch because of its historical significance and reputation for peace. The ADC candidate recalled the promises he made during his previous campaign, saying he had returned to reaffirm his commitment to those pledges, particularly his promise to tackle insecurity if elected president. He also called on Nigerians to turn out in large numbers on election day and vote for the ADC, expressing confidence in the party’s political mission. The rally marks the formal commencement of Atiku’s presidential campaign activities in Sokoto ahead of the 2027 general election. item.title: Valverde strike snatches Real Madrid late win at AEK Athens
item.description: Federico Valverde lashed home a stunning effort from distance to snatch Real Madrid a late 3-2 victory at AEK Athens on Wednesday in the Champions League and preserve their 100 percent start. Jose Mourinho’s side twice came from behind against the Greek champions before Valverde claimed all three points for his side, level with holders Paris Saint-Germain on four wins from four league phase games. Aboubakary Koita sent AEK ahead after 12 minutes and Jude Bellingham equalised with a sublime flick for the record 15-time winners. Stavros Pilios sent the Greek champions ahead with 15 minutes to go but Kylian Mbappe swiftly pulled Madrid level once again, setting the stage for Valverde’s late winner. “Fede has that capability… (but) I didn’t ask him to shoot,” Mourinho told Movistar about his match-winner, who came on in the second half. “I told him was that the game was wide open, it was being played at great speed… a fresh player like Fede, with his ability to cover a lot of ground, I told him to attack the space and arrive in the dangerous areas.” Madrid have now won seven straight games across all competitions. “We fought for (the victory), and with the score at 2–2 we didn’t settle,” added Mourinho. “It would always be an acceptable result, we’d be on 10 points, but we wanted more.” Mourinho started with Vinicius Junior on the left flank, after he missed the team’s previous two matches through suspension, in La Liga. The hosts started with huge energy at the Agia Sophia stadium and it was not overly surprising when they took an early lead. Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois saved well from former Los Blancos striker Luka Jovic before Koita sent AEK ahead. The Mauritanian winger shifted cleverly inside Marc Cucurella and thumped home at the near post, catching out Courtois. The Belgian goalkeeper saved again from Jovic as AEK tried to make their strong start count. However they inevitably began to tire and Madrid began to take the reins in the Greek capital. Kylian Mbappe fired over and Bellingham netted from close range but was shown to be offside. Moments later the England international scored again and nobody could deny him this one. Cucurella fired in a low cross and Bellingham produced a brilliant flicked finish to beat goalkeeper Alberto Brignoli. Former Chelsea defender Cucurella tested Brignoli and Bernardo Silva nodded off-target before the interval as Mourinho’s team controlled the game. Brignoli pushed away Eder Militao’s long-range effort early in the second half and Lazaros Rota blocked superbly to deny the heavily-involved Cucurella. – Another fightback – Mbappe bent a shot narrowly wide of the top corner with Italian stopper Brignoli at full stretch. The France forward was frustrated by the AEK defence when Vinicius turned sharply and found him with a high pass, but the striker’s shot was blocked. item.description: Former Osun State Governor Olagunsoye Oyinlola has said President Bola Tinubu and former Vice President Atiku Abubakar should retire from active politics and allow younger Nigerians to take over the country’s leadership. Oyinlola, a member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), said he supports Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, who is seeking the presidency on the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), for the 2027 election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, the former governor argued that age should be a consideration in determining who seeks public office. “When I was in Osun, I made a declaration based on my experience in office that anybody above 50 should not aspire to be governor of a state,” Oyinlola said. item.title: Tinubu Returns To Abuja After Umrah In Saudi Arabia
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has returned to Abuja after performing the Umrah pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia. The President’s aircraft landed at the Presidential Wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport at 8:53 p.m. on Wednesday. He was received on arrival by the Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila; the Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa; the Minister of State for Defence; the Inspector-General of Police and other government officials. ﻿ Tinubu departed King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, at 5:13 p.m. Saudi time after completing the lesser Hajj in Makkah. Before his departure, the President held a brief meeting with the Deputy Governor of Makkah Region, Prince Saud bin Mishal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, at the Royal Guest Palace within the airport. During the visit, Tinubu led members of the Nigerian delegation in performing the Umrah rites, including the circumambulation of the Holy Ka’abah. He was also granted the privilege of entering the Holy Ka’abah on Sunday, where he and members of his delegation performed two raka’at prayers. According to a statement by his spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, the President offered prayers for Nigeria’s peace, security, unity and prosperity, as well as divine guidance and wisdom for the country’s leaders. His entourage included the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, and the governors of Sokoto, Jigawa, Kaduna, Borno and Yobe States, among others. item.title: Rainbow Coalition: Tinubu tells Nasarawa supporters to vote only APC candidates
item.description: Edwin Philip, Lafia President Bola Tinubu has charged his supporters in Nasarawa State to vote for only the candidates of All Progressives Congress during the forthcoming 2027 general elections. President Tinubu stated this during the APC Presidential Campaign rally which was held on Wednesday in Lafia, the Nasarawa State capital. The president who was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima noted that voting candidates of the party would help to sustain the renewed hope agenda of the present administration at all levels of government. According to him, Nasarawa State had witnessed tremendous developments under his watch as President including the construction and rehabilitation of roads, healthcare facilities, schools, among others. Soliciting for the renewal of his mandate come 2027, he appealed to residents of the state to give him another opportunity to lead the country for another four years, by voting for him, promising to do more for the people. “We want to assure you that if God wills and we win the upcoming elections, we will see that we support you for maximum safety. We call on you to vote for all our party’s candidates. The biggest message from the leader of the country is: APC from top to bottom, APC from bottom to top. ​ “We do not want a situation where they say vote for the president and not the governor, or vote for the governor and not the president, or the senator, or the House of Assembly. ​ “We want APC straight! APC straight! APC from top to bottom and bottom to top. May God give us peace and understanding. May God grant us peace of mind. We thank you very much,” he emphasised. He further commended the Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule for embarking on people oriented projects that have transformed the living conditions of the people for the better. On his part, the Chairman of the All Progressives Governors Forum and Governor of Imo State, Hope Uzodinma highlighted the benefits of the economic policies of President Bola Tinubu, urging the people to ensure that the President returned to power for another four years in order to deliver more dividends of democracy. “It is our decision to continue the deliberate trajectory of Nigeria through the architect of modern Nigeria, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. “We have come to Nasarawa State, we have seen the developments. We have seen that through the Renewed Hope Agenda, the Hope of Nasarawa State is renewed. “And we are here to affirm once more that Nigeria is in good hands, that all of you should vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, “We have worked so hard, we have 31 governors, the party is a family, we plead for peace, we plead for harmony, we plead for a peaceful Nigeria. Support our president, support our governorship candidate, support Nigeria. May God bless all of us as we support the All Progressives Congress,” he said. item.title: 2Baba ends six-year album wait, announces ‘Oldest Young Man’ release date
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Nigerian music star, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has announced November 27, 2026, as the release date for his forthcoming album, ‘Oldest Young Man’, his first studio project in six years. The singer announced the date in a post on his Instagram handle on Tuesday, describing the project as timeless music. “The legacy continues. OLDEST YOUNG MAN drops 27.11.26. Timeless music, no expiration date,” he wrote. View this post on Instagram The announcement comes after months of teasing the album on social media, with 2Baba repeatedly using its title in his Instagram captions. In August, he wrote: “I’ve lived it, I’ve seen it, I’m still here. My new album, Oldest Young Man, soon come.” On his birthday, the singer also described himself as the “forever the oldest young man”. The upcoming project will be his first album since ‘Warriors’, released in 2020, which was his eighth studio album. 2Baba first rose to prominence in the 1990s, composing jingles before co-founding the music group Plantashun Boiz with Blackface and Faze in 1996. He later established himself as one of the pioneers of Afropop, influencing generations of Nigerian artistes with his music. His album releases include ‘Face 2 Face’ (2004), ‘Grass 2 Grace’ (2006), ‘The Unstoppable’ (2009), ‘The Unstoppable International Edition’ (2010), ‘Away and Beyond’ (2012), ‘The Ascension’, ‘Rewind, Select, Update’ (2015) and ‘Warriors’ (2020). item.title: Liverpool collapse to Champions League defeat at Fenerbahce
item.description: Dirk Kuyt got the better of his former club Liverpool as Fenerbahce twice came from behind for a famous 3-2 win in Istanbul that breathed new life into their Champions League campaign. Liverpool had won their opening three European games under Andoni Iraola, but were punished for sloppy defending in a surprise defeat. Trey Nyoni and substitute Alexander Isak twice put the visitors in front. But Liverpool, who lost twice away to Galatasaray last season, were beaten again in Istanbul as Englishmen Mason Greenwood and Archie Brown levelled before Vedat Muriqi’s winner. Fenerbahce’s interim boss Kuyt, who spent six years at Anfield as a player, was taking charge for just the second time after Ismail Kartal quit last week. The Turkish giants had taken just two points from their opening three Champions League games but made the most of Liverpool’s generosity at the back. Liverpool’s perfect Champions League start allowed Iraola the luxury of leaving out Isak and Florian Wirtz among five changes from Sunday’s 1-0 defeat by Arsenal. Nyoni retained his place and capped another fine performance with his first Liverpool goal from the edge of the box. Just four minutes later, though, Alisson Becker was deceived by Greenwood’s deflected free-kick to equalise. Iraola unleashed Isak, Wirtz and Cody Gakpo from the bench just after the hour mark and got an almost immediate reward. Isak was afforded far too much space to head in Gakpo’s cross. But again Liverpool quickly handed back their advantage. Gakpo’s touch inadvertently deflected a cross beyond Alisson to give Brown an easy tap-in at the back post. Liverpool then conceded for the 10th time in four Champions League games when Muriqi outmuscled Jeremy Jacquet to a looping cross and steered a header into the bottom corner. Defeat cost Liverpool the chance to move level with Paris Saint-Germain at the top of the Champions League table as they sit. Victory moves Fenerbahce move up to 19th in the 36-team table.
